headline: Europe's largest industrial carbon-capture facility inaugurated at Yara Sluiskil, feeding the Northern Lights cross-border chain
summary: Yara opened a facility at its Sluiskil ammonia plant in the Netherlands capturing and liquefying up to 800,000 t/yr of CO2 and shipping it via Northern Lights vessels to Oygarden, Norway, for storage ~2,600 m below the seabed (~12 Mt over 15 years); billed as the first complete cross-border CCS value chain.
co2crc_note: A live, operating template for capturing hard-to-abate industrial (ammonia) CO2 and monetising a capture-in-one-country, store-in-another chain, directly analogous to Australia's cross-border ambitions (Bayu-Undan, Australia-Japan/Korea export concepts).

headline: Airhive and Australian Carbon Vault win federal funding to build Australia's first DAC-and-storage hub
summary: UK DAC developer Airhive and Australian Carbon Vault secured ~A$10m (US$7.2m) of Australian Government funding, part of a ~A$32.6m carbon-removal awards round, to build Australia's first integrated direct-air-capture-and-storage hub, pairing Airhive's fluidised-bed capture with onshore geological storage in South Australia's Arckaringa Basin.
co2crc_note: Home-jurisdiction, first-of-a-kind DACCS deployment coupling engineered removal to Australian onshore storage (Arckaringa Basin) - squarely in CO2CRC's technical/storage-characterisation wheelhouse and a marker of federal appetite to fund durable CDR.
extractor_note: Award to Airhive/ACV stated as A$10m (US$7.2m); the ~A$32.6m is the wider awards round, not this item's amount. Page-fetch blocked by egress proxy; date confirmed via search corroboration.

headline: Switzerland launches Europe's first commercial cross-border BECCS chain, shipping biogenic CO2 to Greensand in Denmark
summary: Airfix, CO2 Energie AG and South Pole began transporting liquefied biogenic CO2 (up to ~4,300 t/yr) from the Regionalwerke AG Baden biomethane plant in Niederwil to INEOS-operated Project Greensand for permanent North Sea storage, at ~92% net removal efficiency.
co2crc_note: Early working template for small-volume, ISO-container cross-border CO2 export chains under the London Protocol - relevant to Australia's export-and-store concepts.
extractor_note: Radar (2 Sep, just outside the 5-8 Sep daily window). Page-fetch blocked by egress proxy; date confirmed via search corroboration.

headline: Finland's Ministerial Finance Committee backs EUR70m biogenic carbon-capture plant at Metsa Fibre's Rauma pulp mill
summary: The panel endorsed state aid for a planned 100,000 t/yr biogenic CO2 capture unit at Metsa Fibre's Rauma pulp mill, feeding renewable e-fuels - a political milestone ahead of a final binding subsidy decision.
co2crc_note: European government backing for point-source biogenic capture at a pulp mill; a comparator for durable-CDR public-support design.
extractor_note: Radar (4 Sep, outside window). EUR70m is the plant's stated investment cost, not the aid sum (the state-aid amount is not clearly stated); flagged for review. Page-fetch blocked by egress proxy.

headline: Sinopec, Kazakhstan and Nazarbayev University launch a low-carbon/CCUS cooperation initiative in Astana
summary: Announced around the 2026 International CCUS Technology Conference (1-2 Sep, Astana), the Initiative for Cooperation on Low-Carbon Energy Development calls for closer collaboration on CCUS technologies and standards across China, Kazakhstan, the UK, US and Canada.
co2crc_note: Sinopec extending CCUS standard-setting reach into Central Asia; a signal on where Chinese CCUS diplomacy and standards are heading.
